source_line: Source: 2026 Norton Insights Report: Holiday Scams (released Nov. 5, 2026)
caption:
Chasing a Black Friday deal could cost you about $394.

A new Norton survey of 1,000 US adults, fielded Sept. 10–21, 2026, finds nearly 1 in 6 US adults (16%) have been scammed while holiday shopping online — and 88% of those victims lost money, an average of $394 each. It's not just the careless: 35% say they bought from a seller they suspected might be a scam because the deal was too good to pass up, and 72% admit holiday deals sway them.

My take: "too good to pass up" is exactly how the trap is baited. A price that makes no sense is the warning, not the reason to click. Slow down before you type a card number into a site you've never heard of.

Have you spotted a holiday deal that looked too good to be true? 👇
